transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, I guess what finally made me make the appointment is that I keep messing up these basic adult-life things that everyone else seems to just, like, do. I’ll forget to pay a bill even if I know it exists, or I’ll open an email about an interview and think, “I need to respond to that,” and then somehow days go by and I just… don’t. Or I’ll have an appointment and it’s in my calendar, but I still miss it or remember too late.

It’s not just small stuff anymore. I keep dropping errands halfway through or meaning to follow up on things and then realizing I never did, and now it’s actually costing me opportunities. Like interviews or things that could’ve helped me get my life moving. It feels embarrassing because I have a bachelor’s degree and I’m supposed to be able to handle this, but I keep forgetting the kind of things that really matter.
When you think back to childhood, were you already having trouble with things like remembering assignments, staying organized, or following through on tasks?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t like this just started now. Even in elementary school, my teachers would write these comments that were basically like, “She’s bright, but…” and then there was always a whole list after the “but.”

I lost worksheets constantly. Like, I’d swear I had it, or I’d remember doing part of it, but then when it was time to turn it in, it would just be gone in my backpack or my desk or who knows where. My desk was honestly kind of infamous, I think. It would get so packed with papers and random stuff that I couldn’t find assignments even when they were literally in there somewhere.

And I remember rushing through directions a lot, too. Like I’d start before fully understanding what I was supposed to do, and then I’d have to redo things or I’d miss parts of the assignment. Teachers also said I talked out of turn a lot. Not always trying to be disruptive, but I’d have a thought and just say it before I could stop myself.

So, yeah… the organization and follow-through stuff was there really early. It just looked like messy desks and missing worksheets back then.
When you try to read something you need to focus on, do you often find your mind drifting off even when you want to pay attention?

Yeah, all the time. It’s honestly one of the most frustrating things because I can sit down fully intending to focus, like, “Okay, I’m going to update my resume now,” or “I’m going to work through this coding practice problem,” and then it’s like my attention just gets yanked away.

Sometimes it’s something obvious, like a text notification pops up and I think I’ll just glance at it for one second, and then suddenly I’m replying or checking something else. Or if someone is talking outside my room, even if I’m trying not to listen, my brain just locks onto it. But it’s not always external stuff. Sometimes it’s just a random thought, like I’ll remember another task I should do, and then I’m off in that direction before I even realize I stopped reading or working.

And then I’ll kind of “come to” and notice the resume is still sitting there half-edited, or the coding problem is still on the screen and I’ve made no progress. It’s not that I don’t care. I do care. I’m trying to pay attention. It just feels like my mind slips away really easily, even when I’m telling myself not to.
When you’re doing something that’s genuinely interesting or enjoyable to you, do you still have trouble staying focused?

Yeah… I do. I mean, it’s a little better if I’m genuinely into the thing, but it’s not like interest magically fixes it.

Like with coding practice problems, sometimes I do actually enjoy them once I get into it, especially if it feels like a puzzle. Or updating my resume can feel motivating because I’m thinking, okay, this could actually help me get a job or an interview. But even then, I’ll sit down to do it and something tiny can pull me completely away. A text notification pops up, and I’ll think, “I’ll just check what it says,” and then I’m not just checking it — I’m responding, then maybe looking at something related, and then suddenly I realize the resume or the coding problem is still sitting there and I haven’t touched it in, like, twenty minutes.

Or if someone’s talking outside my room, even if it’s not important and I’m trying not to listen, my brain kind of grabs onto it. I’ll lose the thread of what I was doing. And sometimes it’s not even something outside of me — it’ll be a random thought, like, “Oh, I need to do that other thing,” and before I’ve really decided anything, I’m halfway into thinking about that instead.

So yes, even with things I care about or like, I can get pulled off track really easily, and a lot of the time I don’t notice it until after I’ve already drifted.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I guess it depends what you mean by unwanted thoughts.

I definitely get random thoughts popping in, like things I suddenly remember or worries about stuff I need to do, but I don’t know if I’d describe them as intrusive in the sense of, like, thoughts that keep forcing themselves into my mind over and over. It’s more like my mind jumps around a lot, and sometimes I’m annoyed by it because I’m trying to focus on something else.

But if you mean thoughts that feel really disturbing or that I can’t get rid of even though I’m trying not to think them… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that as a major thing. At least not in a way that stands out to me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I definitely get frustrated and overwhelmed with myself sometimes, especially when I’m trying to get things done and it feels like I can’t, but I don’t know if I’d call it feeling depressed most days.

Like, I wouldn’t say I wake up every day feeling really low or hopeless or anything like that. It’s more that my mood can dip when I’m stressed or when I feel like I’m falling behind. But “down or depressed most days” doesn’t feel like the main thing I’ve noticed, if that makes sense.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of worrying about a bunch of different things all the time for no clear reason.

I mean, I do worry when there’s something actually happening or something I’ve put off, like if I know I need to deal with something and I haven’t, then it’ll bother me. But I wouldn’t say I’m constantly sitting around worrying about every possible thing, like health, money, family, the future, random disasters, all of that at once. It’s more tied to specific situations.

Sometimes I can get stuck thinking about something because I know I should be handling it, but I don’t know if that counts as “worrying a lot” or if it’s just me being stressed about the thing that’s right in front of me. So… I guess my answer is no, not really, or at least I haven’t noticed that as a major pattern.
Do you often feel physically restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the things I notice a lot.

If I have to sit through something where I’m supposed to just be still and pay attention, like an interview or a meeting or even a movie, I get this really uncomfortable feeling in my body. It’s not just “I’m bored,” exactly. It’s more like this pressure building up inside, like I need to move or get up or shift positions or do something with my hands. If I try to sit totally still, it starts to feel almost unbearable, like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

I’ll keep changing how I’m sitting, crossing and uncrossing my legs, playing with my fingers, touching my hair, picking at something, anything like that. And I’m aware of it, too, which makes it awkward, because part of me is trying to look normal and stay still, but another part of me feels like I physically can’t keep my body quiet for that long.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I still like the things I usually like once I actually start doing them, if that makes sense.

Sometimes I don’t get around to doing things I enjoy, or it feels weirdly hard to start them, and then I can go a while without doing something fun and think, “Why am I not doing anything?” But it doesn’t feel like I’ve stopped caring about them or like they don’t feel good anymore. It’s more like getting myself to begin is the hard part.

Like if a friend suggests something or I finally sit down with something I like, I can enjoy it. So I wouldn’t say I’ve lost pleasure in things. It’s just inconsistent, I guess.
